full_judgment:
Khademul Islam Chowdhury, J: Rule was issued at the instance of the informant calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned orders dated 7.1.2004 and 27.1.2004 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong granting bail to the accused parties in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1260 of 2003 and 61 of 2004 respectively corresponding to G.R. Case No.925 of 2003, arising out of Khulshi P.S. Case No. 15(10)03 should not be cancelled and accused opposite parties be remanded in custody till disposal of the Case. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his order dated 9.11.2003 granted ad-interim bail to accused-opposite party No.1 Mujibar Rahman alias Mujib and after hearing granted regular bail by order dated 7.01.2004. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his order dated 15.1.2004 granted bail to accused-opposite party No.2 Md. Shah Selim alias Sani after hearing both sides granted regular bail to him on 27.01.2004. 

 2. The case for the prosecution in short is that on 16.10.2003 the informant petitioner Mrs. Shilpi Rani Sarker lodged a First Information Report with Khulshi police station on which Khulshi Police Station Case No.15 dated 16.10.2003 under Section 406/420/ 335/386/34 of the Penal Code was started implicating accused opposite party no.1 Md. Mujibur Rahman alias Mujib and accused-opposite party Md. Shah Alam alias Sani alleging inter alia that in the name of sale of feat of Sani Tower Development Tower company the accused-opposite parties cheated defrauded the purchasers by collecting illegal tolls from them. After sale of three flats to the informant on payment of consideration and execution and registration of three sale deeds on 22.3.2001 but withholding the delivery of possession of the flats the accused-opposite parties themselves as also through his un-known miscreants demanded large sum of money as tolls from the petitioner informing her not to handover possession unless the amount was paid and also threatened to kill her husband. Accused No.2 by introducing him as top terror of Chittagong told that he would kill them through his cadre and send to India and she was forced to sign blank stamp paper on her refusal to sign accused-opposite party and other unknown accused prepared to shoot by fixing revolver on her head and she became compelled to sign blank stamps. Accused-opposite party also snatched golden chain weighing 2½ tolas from her neck. Police arrested accused-opposite party no.1 on 22.10.2003 and forwarded him to court with prayer for granting 7 days remand in police custody for recovery of the robbed goods from the accused and for interrogation. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong by impugned order dated 9.11.2003 granted ad-interim bail to accused opposite party No. 1 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1260 of 2004 fixing 24.11.2003 for hearing of the bail matter ignoring the pendency of prayer for remand by the police. Subsequently the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge Chittagong by the impugned order dated 7.1.2004 granted regular bail without considering the gravity of the offences and the terrorists nature of the accused and attending facts and circumstances of the case as well as the stiff opposition by the State. Thereafter accused opposite party no. 2 also filed another Criminal Miscellaneous Case being No.61 of 2004 before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong who was pleased to grant ad-interim bail by impugned order dated 15.01.2004 which was subsequently confirmed by the impugned order dated 27.1.2004 without properly considering the gravity of the offence and the attending facts and circumstances of the case and also strong opposition made by the state as well. 

 6. The informant petitioner filed an application before the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong stating inter alia that the accused opposite parties are men of dangerous, desperate and notorious character and terrorists of the locality and they are constantly holding out threats to the informant petitioner, her husband, as well as other members of her family to their peaceful life. As a result the petitioner has been compelled to keep herself within her residence; the accused opposite parties constantly held out threats to the informant petitioner and her husband over telephone and they are also putting them in an unrelenting pressure to withdraw the case filed against them; the accused opposite parties are also threatening the witnesses of the petitioner urging upon them not to depose in the case against them, else they would have to face dire consequences. 

 7. It is also submitted by the informant that due to aforesaid notorious activities of the accused opposite parties it will be impossible for the prosecution to adduce evidence in the case if the accused-opposite parties are not immediately remanded in custody. Since robbed golden chain and non-Judicial Stamps which have been snatched away by the accused opposite parties are not recovered from the accused parties impugned order of granting ad-interim bail and its subsequent confirmation is unwarranted; Furthermore prosecution prayer for remand awaiting disposal with proven misuse of privilege of bail is still pending and in view of the proven charge of misuse, the learned court ought not to confirm the ad-interim bail. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong completely ignoring the convincing documentary evidence, proven gross misuse of the privilege of bail, most illegally confirmed the bail of the said accused opposite parties. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned orders dated 9.11.2003 and 7.1.2004 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1260 of 2003 and order dated 15.1.2004 and 27.1.2004 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.61 of 2004 granting ad-interim bail to the accused opposite parties and also confirming the same the petitioner moved this court with an application under section 497(I) read with section 439 and 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

 9. Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned advocate assisted by Md. Abdur Rahman advocate appearing for the accused petitioner after taking us through the F.I.R. annexure-`A' and prayer for remand made by the police vide order dated 6.11.2000 annexure-`B' order of ad-interim bail dated 9.11.2003 and order of regular bail dated 7.1.2004 (annexure-'C' and `D') charge sheet dated 22.11.2003 (annexure-`E') G.D. Entry No.775 dated 12.11.2003, inquiry report made by the police dated 16.11.2003 and the prosecution report dated 18.11.2003 (Annexure-I) and order dated 2.12.2003 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (Annexure-J) thereon submits that in view of the nature and gravity of the offences and allegation of direct involvement of the accused opposite parties in a dare-devil manner the accused opposite parties deserve no concession of bail. The learned advocate further submits in view of the prosecution report submitted by the police that the accused opposite parties belonging to a gang of terrorists of dangerous and desperate character grossly misused the privilege of bail it is imperative in the interest of justice that the bail of the accused opposite parties be cancelled and they should be taken into custody immediately. The learned advocate again submits that on the face of constant threat to the opposite parties and their witnesses held out by the accused opposite parties not to depose in the case against them, in gross misuse and abuse of privilege of bail the accused opposite parties disentitled themselves to continue the privilege of bail and as such their bail is liable to be cancelled for the ends of justice. The learned advocate empathically submits that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong in granting bail to the opposite parties totally ignored the gravity of the offence and heinous activities of the accused-opposite parties as disclosed in the prosecution report and considering the cogent and over whelming circumstances pointing to the dangerous desperate nature and character of the accused-parties and continuing threat to the informant and his witnesses their bail are liable to be cancelled. The learned advocate strenuously submits that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong acted illegally in granting bail ignoring the facts that an application praying for remand of the accused the recovery of the robbed non-judicial stamps and the golden chain allegedly snatched away by the accused opposite parties confirmation of the bail is unwarranted and as such their bail should be cancelled. 

 13. In view of the specific allegations in the F.I.R. implicating the accused-opposite parties in the name of a business for sale of flats are cheating the purchasers and also extortion of money from them forcibly and illegally and the prosecution report submitted by the police in non F.I.R. case No.599/03 under section 506 of the Penal Code, Annexure-I alleging that accused-opposite parties are recognized terrorists and extortionists having fire arms in their control and possession and they are habitual offenders and commission of alleged offences of cheating kidnapping and killing are not unusual. Accused-opposite party no.1 after his release on ad-interim bail on 9.11.2003 along with accused opposite party No.2 and 3/4 unknown armed persons came to her residence on 12.11.2003 at 11.45 hours and enquired about her husband calling them as executionist for causing death of her husband, demanded five lacs taka as subscription and two lacs as cost of litigation and threatened to kill the informant and her husband and other family members. As a result the owner residents of the binding including its care takers who lived became panic stricken and lived in uncertainty. The allegations revealed in the F.I.R. charge sheet and the prosecution report annexures 'A, B and I' appear grave and indicate sufficient and over whelming circumstances that the accused opposite parties are men of dangerous and desperate character and after getting ad-interim bail upon assurance to the court to compromise the matter amicably they grossly misused the privilege of bail and they forfeited their right to the enjoyment of the concession of bail. On going through the impugned order it appears that the learned Sessions Judge granted ad-interim bail and confirmed the bail without considering the materials on record and also ignoring the objection raised by the prosecution. It appears the allegation of misuse of the privilege has not been controverted and denied by the accused-opposite parties. It further appears that informant petitioner submitted application for cancellation of ad-interim bail enlarged upon the accused at the time of hearing and grievance was made by the learned advocate for the informant that the accused-opposite parties neither handed over possession of the flats nor returned the money but still held out threats for which she had to lodge general diary against the accused opposite parties at the Thana. 

 15. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge without considering the allegations on either side and applying his judicial mind to the legal aspects confirmed bail of the accused opposite parties 1-2 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos.1260 of 2003 and 61 of 2004 respectively in a shop shot manner. 

 16. Considering all the above aspects we are of opinion elements of misuse of the privilege of bail eminently exist due to terror threat of the accused opposite parties and armed miscreants to withdraw the case and also not to depose prosecution will not have a fair deal at the trial and to enable the informant and her witnesses to depose in the case the bail of the accused-opposite parties should be cancelled and remanded in jail custody till disposal of the case. 

 18. The impugned orders dated 7.1.2004 and 27.1.2004 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong in granting bail to the accused opposite parties bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1260 of 2003 and 61 of 2004 respectively corresponding to G.R. Case No.925 of 2003 arising out of Kulshi P.S Case No. 15(10)2003 under section 406/420/385/386/380/34 of the penal Code be and the same are hereby cancelled. 

 19. The accused-opposite parties No.1 and 2 are hereby directed to surrender to their bail bonds before the learned Metropolitan Session Judge, Chittagong at once they be remanded in jail custody. In case the accused opposite party Nos. 1-2 fail to surrender the Deputy Commissioner and the superintendent of police Chittagong are directed to take appropriate steps to secure their arrest and send them to jail custody.
